abstract: Grapevine (Vitis vinifera) is susceptible to numerous fungal and oomycete pathogens. Plant defense inducers (PDIs) offer the potential to reduce the use of chemical fungicides in viticulture, but their efficacies under vineyard conditions remain variable. Here, we investigated whether alleviating the repression of immune responses could enhance PDI-induced protection against grapevine diseases. We first characterized two grapevine HD2-type histone deacetylases, VvHD2a and VvHD2b, as negative regulators of basal immunity. Their constitutive expression in Arabidopsis thaliana attenuated the flg22-induced oxidative burst and defense-related gene expression, while increasing susceptibility to Botrytis cinerea. The histone deacetylase inhibitor, sodium butyrate (NaBut), blocked this enhanced susceptibility. In grapevine, NaBut alone protected against B. cinerea but did not against Plasmopara viticola. However, combining NaBut with low doses of the PDI Belvine conferred protection against P. viticola comparable to that achieved with the full recommended PDI dose, with a synergistic interaction between both treatments. Similarly, NaBut enhanced Belvine-induced signaling events, such as MAPK phosphorylation and transcriptomic analysis revealed amplified expression of genes involved in multiple defense-related processes. Finally, field trials conducted in two Bourgogne vineyards showed that adding NaBut to a reduced-copper program incorporating Belvine improved downy mildew control on leaves and bunches, with Bayesian probabilities of improved protection ranging from 91% to 95%. Disease severity was comparable to that achieved with the full copper dosage. These findings highlight the potential of combining defense induction by a reduced dosage of PDI and disinhibition to improve PDI-induced disease control while reducing copper inputs in viticulture
